label: Non-concrete cause of an actual concretum's esse
definition: SomeEsseCauseNonConcrete m w CausesIn esse holds when there are distinct c and x such that x is concrete and exists at w, c causes x's esse, c exists at w, and c is not concrete. Ordinary meaning: what makes some concrete thing be is itself not a concrete thing. Example: a Form, or a governing law, as cause of a concrete thing's being. It does not say the cause is absent, and leaves open whether the selected relation holds between the two.
note: Analyst framework definition of a rival position; attribution deferred. Motivated by Platonic Forms or governing laws of nature as causes of being. Rival of EsseCauseIsActualConcreteGround on the same Profile, world, CausesIn and esse. Stronger than the negation: it fixes that the concreteness clause of the bridge fails. The other ways the bridge can fail (an absent cause; a present concrete cause that is not a selected-relation ground) are separate rivals, not recorded here.
